headline: The Philippines wins the first Eurovision Asia

sources.title: Philippines win inaugural Eurovision Asia, Thailand takes runner-up (Bangkok Post)
PH wins Asian edition of Eurovision songfest (The Manila Times)
Philippines: CARMELLE Wins Eurovision Song Contest Asia 2026 (Eurovoix)

chunks.text: A 19-year-old singer from the Philippines has won the first Eurovision Song Contest Asia. The final took place in Bangkok, the capital of Thailand, on November 14, 2026. Eurovision is a [[yearly]] song contest between countries. It began in Europe in 1956. The new Asian [[version]] {{brought together}} singers from 11 countries, including South Korea, Vietnam and Nepal. Thailand {{put on}} the show as the [[host country]]. The show {{kicked off}} with a performance that [[celebrated]] Bangkok.

verbs.correct: To gather people from many places
verbs.wrong: To sing the same song as a group
verbs.why: The school fair brings together families from the whole town. Music often brings people together. The new Asian version of Eurovision brought together singers from 11 countries.

verbs.correct: To organize and present a show
verbs.wrong: To give points to a song
verbs.why: Our school puts on a play every spring. The city puts on a big fireworks show on New Year's Eve. Thailand put on the first Eurovision Asia as the host country.
The game kicks off at seven. The festival kicks off with a parade. The show in Bangkok kicked off with a performance that celebrated the city.

chunks.text: Half of the result came from [[national juries]], groups of [[music experts]] in each country. The other half came from viewers. People in the rest of the world could vote too. Fans could {{tune in}} on YouTube. The singer {{racked up}} 93 points from the juries and 118 from viewers. Her points {{added up to}} 211, and she was first with both groups. A [[duo]] from Thailand {{came in}} second with 170 points.

verbs.correct: To watch a TV or online show
verbs.wrong: To meet a singer in person
verbs.why: Millions of people tune in for the big game. My parents tune in to the news every morning. Fans around the world could tune in on YouTube.
Our best player racks up a lot of points in every game. Good students rack up points in class quizzes. The singer racked up 93 points from the juries and 118 from viewers.
Small savings add up to a lot of money. His two test scores add up to 150. Her points added up to 211.

verbs.correct: To finish at a certain position
verbs.wrong: To sing a song very loudly
verbs.why: He usually comes in first in school races. Our team often comes in last, but we have fun. A duo from Thailand came in second with 170 points.

chunks.text: Her song's name means "Too Much." One of its [[songwriters]] said it is about women's power. That songwriter said women in the Philippines face [[expectations]] that nobody can {{live up to}}. Women who are strong or [[independent]] are often told that they are too much. The song {{stands up for}} them and turns "too much" into praise. It says people are enough just as they are. After her [[victory]], the singer said she felt [[emotional]].

verbs.wrong: To win a prize for hard work
verbs.why: The new phone does not live up to the ads. Many kids work hard to live up to their parents' hopes. One songwriter said women in the Philippines face expectations that nobody can live up to.
Good friends stand up for each other. A fair teacher stands up for quiet students. The song stands up for women who are told that they are too much.

chunks.text: The idea of an Asian Eurovision {{goes back}} to 2017, but several plans {{fell through}} after long [[delays]]. The European Broadcasting Union, the group that runs Eurovision, {{teamed up}} with another company to [[launch]] the contest in 2026. The singer received the [[trophy]] from a Bulgarian singer who won the main Eurovision contest in May 2026. Her win earned her a spot at the next main contest, in Bulgaria in May 2027.

verbs.correct: To have started at a past time
verbs.why: Our family recipe goes back to my great-grandmother. This old church goes back to 1850. The idea of an Asian Eurovision goes back to 2017.
Sometimes a house sale falls through at the last minute. Our trip plans often fall through when money is short. Several earlier plans for an Asian Eurovision fell through.

verbs.correct: To join another group for a project
verbs.wrong: To learn the steps of a dance
verbs.why: Two local shops team up for a big sale. Doctors and teachers team up to help sick children. The European Broadcasting Union teamed up with another company to launch the contest.

mainIdea.s: A teenage singer from the Philippines won the first Asian edition of the Eurovision song contest in Bangkok. Her winning song is about women who hear that they are too much.
mainIdea.why: Her points added up to 211, and she was first with both juries and viewers. One songwriter said the song is about women's power.

mainIdea.s: A young Filipino singer took first place at the new contest thanks to votes from fans. The expert judges in each country liked a duo from Thailand better, but the public saved her.
mainIdea.why: Close, but she was first with the juries too. She racked up 93 points from them, more than any other singer.

mainIdea.s: Thailand has agreed to hold the main Eurovision show in Bangkok next spring for the first time. Officials say tickets for the big European event will be sold from early January.
mainIdea.why: Thailand put on the first Eurovision Asia in Bangkok, and a singer from the Philippines won. The next main contest will be in Bulgaria.

tf.s: A singer from the Philippines won the first Eurovision Song Contest Asia.
tf.why: The contest brought together singers from 11 countries, and the 19-year-old singer from the Philippines won.

tf.s: The winner came in first with the juries but not with the public.
tf.why: She was first with both groups. Her jury and public points added up to 211.

tf.s: A duo from the host country, Thailand, came in second.
tf.why: The Thai duo finished second with 170 points, behind the singer from the Philippines.

tf.s: One songwriter said the song is about women's power.
tf.why: She said women in the Philippines face expectations that nobody can live up to.

tf.s: The song tells women to change so that they are less strong.
tf.why: The song stands up for women who are told that they are too much and says they are enough.

tf.s: Several earlier plans for an Asian Eurovision fell through.
tf.why: The idea goes back to 2017, and there were many delays before the contest finally began in 2026.

lines.text: Did you hear that the Philippines won the first Eurovision Asia?
There's an Asian Eurovision now? I had no idea.
Yes, it {{kicked off}} in Bangkok on November 14. It {{brought together}} singers from 11 countries.
Carmelle, a 19-year-old singer from the Philippines. She really [[stole the show]].
Did the judges like her, or just the fans?
Both. She {{racked up}} the most points from the juries and the public, and they {{added up to}} 211. It was a [[clean sweep]].
Wow. Thailand {{put on}} the show, right? How did they do?
Their duo {{came in}} second. I watched it live. Anyone could {{tune in}} on YouTube.
"Sobra-Sobra." It means "Too Much," but [[in a good way]].
One songwriter said women face expectations that nobody can {{live up to}}. The song {{stands up for}} them.
I love that. She must be [[on cloud nine]].
She said she felt very emotional. The idea for this contest {{goes back}} to 2017, but earlier plans {{fell through}}.
So how did it finally happen?
The European Broadcasting Union {{teamed up}} with another company. And her win earned her a spot at the main contest in Bulgaria in May 2027.
Great voice and a great message. She's [[the whole package]].

expressions.def: Used to say that someone got the most attention and praise at an event
ex: The little drummer stole the show at the school concert.
Her funny speech stole the show at the wedding.

expressions.def: A win of every part of a contest or every prize
ex: Our team made a clean sweep of the awards this year.

expressions.def: Used to say that a word that sounds bad is meant as praise
ex: The movie was strange, but in a good way.
His laugh is loud in a good way.
She was on cloud nine when she got the job.

expressions.def: A person who has every good quality you could want
ex: The new coach is smart, kind and fair. He's the whole package.
